articles.title: When Justice Was Served Alongside A Whiskey
articles.content: **编辑说明**：欢迎来到我们的每日常识问题栏目！ **问题**：在距离最近的真实法院200英里之外的西德州，一位酒馆老板（1972年由保罗·纽曼饰演），在1882年毫无法律训练且仅凭一本法律书籍的情况下，成功获得了司法平民审判官的职位，并开始在自己酒馆的柜台后"颁布"公正。这个人是谁？ **提示**：他自称是"佩科斯河以西的法律"，将自己的酒馆兼法庭以他崇拜的一位英国女演员命名，并坚称整个镇也是以她的名字命名的（实际上镇名源自一位铁路工头）。 原文标题：当正义与威士忌一同上桌时 首次出现在 法律界
articles.summary:
Ed. Note: Welcome to our daily feature Trivia Question of the Day!

With the nearest real courthouse a punishing 200 miles away, which West Texas saloonkeeper (portrayed in 1972 by Paul Newman), with no legal training and exactly one law book to his name, got himself installed as justice of the peace in 1882 and started dispensing “justice” from behind his own bar?

Hint: He branded himself “the Law West of the Pecos,” and named his saloon-slash-courtroom after a British actress he idolized, and insisted he’d named the whole town after her too. (It was really named for a railroad foreman.)

articles.title: Schema Markup 2026: The Hidden SEO Boost For Lawyers
articles.content:
结构化数据标记是律所网站中常被忽视的部分，主要因为通过浏览器查看时无法直接看到它。然而，搜索引擎依赖这种标记提供的信息来识别页面上的信息类型并准确分类，以便日后检索。主流回答引擎的大型语言模型（LLMs）也扮演着类似的角色。理解结构化数据标记的工作原理并有效部署它，可以让您的网站在搜索结果中获得优势，超越那些忽视这一机会的竞争对手。

从技术角度来说，schema.org只是用于帮助网络爬虫识别网页内容类型的"标签"系统中的一种。这种系统的正式名称是结构化数据；您可能会看到结构化数据标记用于指代将结构化数据标签应用于网站的过程，或偶尔指标签本身，就像您可能会说完成文档的"标记"并在某些情况下将个别注释和修正视为文档标记的示例一样。

schema.org开发和维护的特定结构化数据系统已经成为行业标准，以至于结构化数据标记几乎等同于结构化数据的使用，就像"Google"一度几乎可以与"网络搜索"互换使用，直到其市场主导地位被基于LLMs的"聊天机器人"搜索工具所削弱。

虽然Google的搜索主导地位受到一定影响（截至本文撰写之时，Google仍然在整体搜索活动中占据最大份额），但schema.org并未受到相同程度的影响。所有目前用于扫描网站和索引其内容的搜索工具仍然至少部分依赖结构化数据来理解每个页面上的"内容"。

网络爬虫通常仍然可以阅读网站上的部分或全部基于文本的内容（媒体文件则不太可靠），但它们可能无法正确分类这些内容。分类中的索引错误使搜索引擎（如Google）和使用聊天机器人界面的"回答引擎"难以识别页面的内容是否与用户查询相关。用律师熟悉的术语来说：没有结构化数据，搜索引擎可能无法确定网站上的信息是否"响应"用户的查询。Google和新的AI回答引擎往往倾向于排除而不是包含可能与特定查询相关或不相关的材料。

由于结构化数据标记的全部目的在于向搜索机器人发出信号，表明它们正在扫描的信息类型（理想情况下还包括网站内不同页面之间的关系），因此显然选择智慧地应用结构化数据标签至关重要。虽然某些结构化数据标签的适用性可能因律所规模和业务类型（如联邦法还是州法）而有所不同，但有几个标签我总是确保客户的网站使用。

LegalService是一种结构化数据"类型"，其在结构化数据层次结构中的位置可以表示为Thing > Place > LocalBusiness > LegalService或Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > LegalService。位于层次结构中较低位置的每个结构化数据类型都会从其父类型继承多个可能的属性，因此LegalService从LocalBusiness、Organization、Place和Thing继承了各自不同的潜在属性集合。

您可以将"继承"的属性视为可继承的选项；它们是可以应用于结构化数据类型的属性，而不是自动应用的属性。例如，LegalService从Organization继承了应用成员属性的选项，因为组织可以成为其他组织的成员（例如许多国家最大的制造商所属的行业协会）。如果您的律所作为实体不属于任何组织，那么您就不需要使用成员属性与LegalService关联。不过，您可能希望通过employee或owner等属性将LegalService与Person关联起来。

即使是独资律所也至少有一个Person类型的项目。许多律所将拥有多个Person项目。这些个人项目不仅可以通过所识别的人物姓名进行区分，还可以通过每个人物在组织中担任的角色进行区分。常见的例子包括jobTitle（这对于非律师的员工生平非常有用）和worksFor；这两个属性都将个人与律所联系起来，但方式不同。数字营销策略师可能会建议您同时使用这两种方法，以便为搜索引擎提供尽可能多的连接点来澄清这些关系。

sameAs不是一种类型，而是一种属性。几乎所有律师的姓名都会出现在其律所网站之外的多个地方。您的州律师协会是最明显的例子之一，但如果您在Avvo或FindLaw上声明了一个个人资料，这些也会被纳入其中。任何维护您个人信息的专业组织都可以作为sameAs的对象。sameAs属性用于表示Thing > Person :: sameAs，后跟与同一人相关的页面的URL，并有助于一个称为实体解析的过程，机器学习系统利用该过程来帮助澄清其他网站上的URL所引用的姓名是否属于您的律所网站上识别的同一人（而不是与同名的人）。

sameAs也可以用于Organization和Person，因此如果您的律所在多个在线平台出现，您可以使用sameAs + URL在整个网站的结构化数据标记中"连接点"。对于律所网站来说，sameAs的目标不仅仅是消除歧义（尽管应用sameAs也可以实现这一功能），还包括权威性。向搜索引擎展示您的律所在其他地方被引用的位置，有助于搜索引擎分类您的其他出现并为这些情况"记功"。

使用结构化数据标记来提高律所网站性能的总体原则适用于所有法律类型。这一原则在传统搜索、AI概述和聊天机器人回答引用中保持一致。然而，您需要与当地的数字营销专家合作，确保律所提供的法律服务得到恰当反映，每位合伙人和律师都有身份识别并链接到各平台和网站上的数字足迹，以及您的位置和联系信息与Google的NAP（名称、地址、电话号码）指南一致。可能还有其他具体需求，需要针对您的律所及其网站添加新帖子和页面的方式进行个性化关注，因此在考虑任何更新时，务必与您信任的律所SEO专家交流。

Annette Choti律师具有超过20年的法律经验，是Law Quill的创始人兼首席执行官，该机构为律所提供精品法律营销服务。Annette撰写了畅销书《点击磁铁：律所数字营销终极指南》，主持热门播客《法律营销休息室》，并创立了Click Magnet Academy，在该学院她教授专业人士如何利用强大的LinkedIn平台。作为律师协会、法律协会和营销会议的受邀演讲者，Annette提供法律营销洞察力，并带来娱乐性的转折。Annette曾从事戏剧和职业喜剧表演，这与法律领域并没有什么不同，如果我们都诚实地说的话。您可以在LinkedIn上找到Annette，或通过电子邮件直接联系她：Annette@LawQuill.com。
articles.summary:
Schema markup is an easily overlooked part of your law firm website, in large part because, if you are viewing the website via web browser, you will never actually see it. Search engines, however, rely on the information this type of markup provides to recognize the types of information located on each page and accurately categorize them for later retrieval. The large language models (LLMs) that drive the leading answer engine chatbots do much the same. Understanding how schema markup works and deploying it effectively across your website gives you an edge over competitors who neglect this opportunity for increasing the “grip” points search tools can use to retrieve relevant pages in response to user queries.

What Is Schema Markup?

Speaking technically for a moment, schema.org is only one version of a type of “tag” system used to help web crawlers recognize the kind of content they should expect to find on a webpage. The formal name for this type of system is structured data; you may sometimes see structured data markup used to refer to the process of applying the structured data tags to a website, or occasionally to the tags themselves, in the same way that you might review to finishing the “markup” of a document or sometimes reference the individual notes and corrections as instances of the document’s markup.

The specific system of structured data developed and maintained by schema.org is so much the industry standard that schema markup is virtually synonymous with the use of structured data in much the same way that “Google” was used almost interchangeably with “web search” until its market dominance was disrupted by the development of “chatbot” search tools powered by LLMs (large language models).

Why Is Schema Markup Important for Law Firm Websites?

While Google has seen inroads on its search dominance (it is worth noting that Google still, as of the time of this writing, captures a greater share of total search activity than any other single tool), schema.org has not been affected in the same way. All of the search tools currently in use for scanning websites and indexing their contents still rely at least partially on structured data to make sense of the “contents” they find on each page.

Web crawlers can usually still read some or all of the text-based content on your website (media files are more iffy) without structured data, but they may not categorize those contents appropriately. Indexing errors in classification make it harder for search (search engines like Google, but also “answer engines” that use a chatbot interface) to recognize when your page contains the kind of information that would likely be relevant to a user’s query. To put this problem in terms familiar to attorneys: Without structured data, search engines may not be able to determine whether the information on your website is “responsive” to a user’s query. Both Google and the newer AI answer engines tend to err on the side of excluding, rather than including, materials that may or may not be responsive to a specific query.

Details: The Schema Tags Your Law Firm Website Needs

Because the whole purpose of schema markup is to signal to search bots what kind(s) of information they are scanning and (ideally) how the distinct pages within a website relate to one another, it is obviously important to choose wisely in applying schema tags to your law firm website. While some schema tags may be more or less applicable, depending on the size of your law firm and the type(s) of work you do (e.g., federal law vs. state only) there are a few tags I always try to make sure my clients’ websites are using.

LegalService

LegalService is a schema “type,” and its place in the schema hierarchy may be structured as either Thing > Place > LocalBusiness > LegalService or Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > LegalService. Each schema type located at a position below the top of the hierarchy will inherit several possible properties from its parent types, so LegalService inherits distinct sets of potential properties from LocalBusiness, Organization, Place, and Thing.

Think of the “inherited” properties as inherited options; they are properties that may be applied to the schema type, not properties that are applied automatically. For instance, LegalService inherits the option to apply a member property from Organization, because organizations can be members of other organizations (think of the industry associations to which many of the nation’s largest manufacturers belong, for instance). If your law firm does not, as an entity, belong to an organization, then you would not use the member property with LegalService. You might, however, want to associate your LegalService with a Person via a property like employee or owner.

Person

Even a solo law firm will have at least one item of the Person type. Many law firms will have several Person items. These individual items can be separated not just by the names of the people identified, but by the role each person fulfills within the organization. Common examples include jobTitle (this one is great to use in staff bios for non-attorneys) and worksFor; both properties connect the individual to the law firm, but in different ways. A digital marketing strategist may advise you to use both to provide search engines with as many points of connection as possible for clarifying these relationships.

sameAs

sameAs is not a type, but a property. Almost all attorneys’ names are listed in multiple places other than their own law firm websites. Your state bar association is one of the most obvious examples, but if you have claimed a profile on Avvo or FindLaw, those would count as well. Any professional organization that maintains an individual entry on you is also fair game. The sameAs property is used to to denote Thing > Person :: sameAs followed by the URL of the page that relates to the same person, and it facilitates a process known as entity resolution, which machine learning systems use to help clarify that the name referenced on an off-site URL belongs to the same person identified on your law firm website (rather than to another person with a similar name). Entity resolution continues evolving along with improvements in natural language processing (NLP), but the current SEO standard, of providing search engines with as many opportunities as practical, looks set to remain a useful strategy for the long haul.

sameAs can be used with Organization as well as with Person, so if your law firm appears in multiple places online, you can “connect the dots” for search engines using sameAs + URL in your schema markup across your website. For law firm websites, the goal of sameAs is not just disambiguation (although applying sameAs can also serve that function), but authority. Showing search engines the other places where your law firm is referenced online helps search engines to categorize your appearances elsewhere and give you “credit” for those instances.

Make Sure You Get Tailored Advice

The general principle of using schema markup to improve your law firm website’s performance holds true regardless of the type of law you practice. It even remains consistent across traditional search, AI overviews, and the citations surfaced with chatbot answers. However, you will want to work with a digital marketing specialist in your area to make sure that the legal services your law firm offers are properly reflected, that each partner and associate is identified and linked to their digital presence across platforms and websites, and that your location and contact information are consistent with Google’s NAP (name, address, phone number) guidelines. There may also be other considerations specific to your law firm and the way you integrate new posts and pages into your website that demand personalized attention, so be sure to talk with a law firm SEO expert you trust as you consider any updates.

Annette Choti, Esq., has over two decades of legal experience and is the Founder & CEO of Law Quill, a concierge legal marketing agency for law firms.  Annette authored the bestselling book Click Magnet: The Ultimate Guide To Digital Marketing For Law Firms, hosts the popular Legal Marketing Lounge podcast, and founded Click Magnet Academy where she teaches professionals to leverage the powerful LinkedIn platform. As a sought after speaker for Bar Associations, Legal Associations, and Marketing Conferences, Annette provides legal marketing insight along with an entertaining twist. Annette used to do theatre and professional comedy, which is not so different from the legal field if we are all being honest. Annette can be found on LinkedIn or directly through email at Annette@LawQuill.com

articles.title: ‘Adventures In Legal Tech’: How One Litigator Uses Claude To Build His Case Strategy
articles.content:
在许多小型律所或独立律师的办公室里，律师们经常在庭审前只能与自己辩论案件，缺乏同事或对手的反馈。与大型律所相比，这些律师可能没有同事与之进行模拟辩论或提供反对意见，这使得他们在庭审中容易忽视案件的弱点。

在最新一期的《法律科技冒险》节目中，诉讼律师路易斯·瓦尔加斯·里韦拉（Luis Vargas Rivera）与主持人贾里德·科雷亚（Jared Correia）探讨了他如何利用AI工具克服这一问题。

**寻找论点的薄弱环节**
瓦尔加斯·里韦拉利用Claude（一个AI工具）开发了一个名为“逆向审查”（Adversarial Review）的技能。这种技能通过预设指令，让Claude在每次输入特定文件或提出特定请求时，都能按照相同的流程进行处理。瓦尔加斯·里韦拉的“逆向审查”技能会让Claude像对手律师一样，针对他的诉讼动议或投诉书中的每一个论点进行反驳或质疑，从而帮助他发现并加强论证中的弱点。

**争夺受众的注意力**
瓦尔加斯·里韦拉还强调，律师的营销策略应该更多地针对其他律师，而非直接面向潜在客户。与争夺高竞争关键词（如“人身伤害”）相比，通过建立与其他律师的转介关系，不仅成本更低，效果也更显著。

想了解更多细节，请收听该期节目。
（原文首发于Above the Law网站）
---

articles.summary:
Most solo and small firm litigators walk into a hearing having only argued their case with themselves. No moot, no devil’s advocate, no one in the room willing to say, “That’s your weakest point, here’s why.” 

In a bigger firm, that’s a colleague down the hall. In a solo practice or small firm, it might be … nobody.

In this episode of “Adventures in Legal Tech,” litigator Luis Vargas Rivera joins host Jared Correia to discuss how he built a workaround. 

Finding Your Argument’s Weak Spot

A Claude skill is a set of instructions you give the AI once, so it repeats the same process every time you mention a specific phrase or hand it a specific type of document. 

Vargas Rivera’s skill, which he calls Adversarial Review, tells Claude exactly how to behave when he asks it to test the arguments in a motion or complaint

Competing for Your Audience

Who else is already reaching your audience, and how likely is your message to cut through?

Marketing toward other lawyers who can become referral sources is often more effective and cheaper than targeting high-demand keywords like “personal injury,”  Vargas Rivera says.

articles.title: Justice Jackson Calls Out The Supreme Court’s Shadow Docket ‘Speed Dial’ For Favored Litigants
articles.content:
Ed. note: Welcome to our daily feature, Quote of the Day.
Why is it that one party should get a fast pass to the Supreme Court of the United States when so many other parties are queued up, waiting patiently for the court’s attention?
— Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, in remarks reported by the ABA Journal, questioning the Supreme Court’s increasingly frequent use of emergency orders. Jackson warned that the emergency docket risks becoming an end run around the ordinary appeals process — a “special avenue” reserved for privileged litigants with the Court on “speed dial” — while imposing corrosive institutional costs on the judiciary and undermining public trust in the Court.
Staci Zaretsky is the managing editor of Above the Law, where she’s worked since 2011. She’d love to hear from you, so please feel free to email her with any tips, questions, comments, or critiques. You can follow her on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Threads, or connect with her on LinkedIn.
